contract: Hard eligibility remains four frames, but the already-observed current input receives an independent fail-closed fifth-frame certificate so an age-four solve tail may retain that input and retry; this certificate cannot authorize a new action.
summary: The default Stage 1 run remained alive with all nine Hard-4 actions at f12135, but one 54.519 ms solve tail aged the snapshot by four frames and exhausted the current-hold certificate, producing unsupported-delivery-age. Repeated native replay of the same 393-bullet snapshot completed Hard-4 in roughly 2.5-5 ms, while the observed current up action remained source-certified through h16; the failure was publication authority during a transient synchronous stall, not an earlier route choice or a modeled dead end. Removing all current bullets, the source-defined spawner, and the enemy preserves the stable h4/h5 authority relation; the full artifact preserves the measured latency tail.
